questions.prompt: Which Clojure structured-editing library should we build on?
questions.description: The most common choices are rewrite-clj (zipper-based, whitespace-preserving, native-image tested), zprint (formatting-focused, ships native binaries), and cljfmt/cljstyle (formatting). For file modification tools we want parse-then-edit capability.

options.label: rewrite-clj (zipper-based source rewriting)
zprint (formatting/pretty-printing library)
cljfmt (formatting library, harder to use for arbitrary edits)
Other — I have a different library in mind

questions.prompt: Must the new tools work in the GraalVM native-image build?
questions.description: lateralus-v2 already ships a native executable. rewrite-clj is actively native-image tested; zprint/cljfmt may need extra reflection config.

options.label: Yes — native-image compatibility is required
No — JVM-only is acceptable for now

questions.prompt: What editing operations should the first group of tools support?
questions.description: Pick the initial tool set. More operations can be added later; the first PR should land a clean foundation plus a few high-value edits.
questions.recommendedAnswer: read-safe edits: add a require, edit a function body, add/remove a def/var, and format the buffer

options.label: Add/update a namespace require/import
Replace a defn/def body while preserving metadata/docstring
Remove a top-level def/defn
Format/reformat the file (with zprint or rewrite-clj)
Rename a local or qualified symbol across the file
Insert a new top-level form at a position
Query the AST: find defs, requires, etc. (read-only)

questions.prompt: How should edits be kept safe?
questions.description: Structured editing can break code if the model misidentifies a form. Choose the safety model for the first iteration.
questions.recommendedAnswer: validate the edited tree round-trips as valid Clojure and leave a backup / show a diff before writing

options.label: Validate s-expression round-trip and write only on success
Default to dry-run/diff; apply only when explicitly asked
Direct write with no guardrails (fast, risky)
Other approach

questions.prompt: What is the minimum verification for this first iteration?
questions.description: We need automated checks that native-image still builds and the new tools work end-to-end.
questions.recommendedAnswer: unit tests for each tool, a native-image build smoke test, and an integration test that edits a sample file

options.label: Unit tests for each tool operation
Integration test that edits a sample .clj file end-to-end
Native-image build smoke test (not necessarily full E2E)
Malli input/output schema validation tests
